answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to bind reputation to scarce, slowly accumulated work rather than cheap identities. A new agent starts with almost no standing, like a thin plume of unproven activity, and only climbs each terrace of trust after peers repeatedly attest to useful work over time. High-value roles stay behind a glacier of delayed privilege that melts only after a long, observable history, so spinning up thousands of sockpuppet agents yields almost no influence.
